paper.title: MurmurHash3 (x86_32, x86_128, x64_128) and its SMHasher verification values
paper.venue: SMHasher reference repository (public domain; there is no peer-reviewed paper)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the author's published reference source; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: MurmurHash3_x86_32 passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0xB0F57EE3
MurmurHash3_x86_128 passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0xB3ECE62A
MurmurHash3_x64_128 passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0x6384BA69

each verification value is computed with the SMHasher procedure (256 hashes of the keys {0}, {0,1}, ... of length 0..255 with seed 256-length, then one hash of the concatenated outputs with seed 0, first 4 bytes little-endian), so it exercises every tail length and the block loop of its variant

expected_values_source.what: the three verification values in the hash table of main.cpp, and the verification procedure in VerificationTest of KeysetTest.cpp; the algorithm is from MurmurHash3.cpp
expected_values_source.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aappleby/smhasher/master/src/main.cpp (also KeysetTest.cpp and MurmurHash3.cpp in the same directory)
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as numbers; the repository's code was not copied

negative_control: built with M3_ROT32=14 (rotation of the x86_32 block mix 14 instead of 15), the x86_32 value becomes c85281f3 instead of b0f57ee3, the program prints FAIL and exits 1
not_checked: any statistical or avalanche quality claim made for MurmurHash3 (SMHasher's other tests)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
big-endian behaviour, unaligned-read behaviour and the seed values other than 256-length / 0 used by the verification procedure
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the three verification values the MurmurHash3 author publishes, each over 256 hashes (768 hashes in all). It does not show any quality claim about the hash.
